thread:
maria: Heads up — cluster-west rtv pool is showing a ~30% throughput drop starting ~11:20 UTC, multiple worker restarts and a spike in GPU OOMs (seen 6 OOMs in last 10m). Dashboard: https://monitoring/redwood/rtv/cluster-west/throughput spike and restart counts. Anyone oncall?
aj: I'm on it. Which model variants and any traffic changes?
maria: Mostly gptx-4f-8k @ v2 model variants. Traffic shows more small single-turn requests (client churn). No config change deployed in last 24h.
kevin: Pasting tail of worker logs from one of the restarted pods (worker-42):
```
2026-03-18T11:22:03Z WARN  allocator: failed to allocate pages: requested=1321205760 bytes
2026-03-18T11:22:03Z ERROR runtime: GPU OOM on device 0, evicting KV cache entries
2026-03-18T11:22:03Z INFO  kvcache: evicted 480 entries (total_size=1.1GB -> 600MB)
2026-03-18T11:22:03Z INFO  gc: hotpage sweep started, slab_rebalancer triggered
2026-03-18T11:22:04Z INFO  worker: restarting due to OOM
```
kevin: Also saw repeated small allocations (~32-256KB) and a backlog of continuous-batch jobs in the same timeslice.
ops-bot: Alert: worker-restart: worker-42 restarted (OOM) — incident created #INC-8472
deng: Kernel selection logs show repeated fallbacks: preferred kernel=fast-fused-attn-v2, fallback=generic-attn. Reason: allocator returned ENOMEM during kernel probe -> runtime switched to safe path which increases memory pressure. Snip: `kernel_picker: probe fast-fused-attn-v2 -> probe failed (alloc_failure) -> fallback to generic-attn`
aj: That smells like memory fragmentation on the device rather than raw usage. Do we have pmap / slab stats from the runtime allocator?
kevin: Uploading quick allocator snapshot:
```
allocator: total_allocated=45.6GB
allocator: total_reserved=52.0GB
slab: free_fragments=1324
slab: largest_free_blob=48MB
slab: active_slabs=1024
kvcache: entries=12000 size=1.8GB
small_alloc_histogram: 0-4KB: 1.2M, 4-32KB: 420k, 32-256KB: 88k
```
kevin: The important bit is large free fragments count and very small largest_free_blob -> fragmentation. Also KV cache churning (lots of evictions) which is causing many small allocations and frees.
leo: Quick mitigation we can try: throttle KV sweep aggressiveness and enable prefix-caching offload to CPU for hottest entries, and temporarily pin kernel selection to alloc-aware kernels so we don't probe failing fast-fused kernels.
aj: Agreed. Steps I propose: 1) canary change on two nodes in cluster-west: set runtime flag `--kernel-preference=alloc-aware` 2) reduce kvcache.sweep_interval from 500ms -> 2000ms and lower kvcache.max_active_evictions=200 3) enable `kvcache.cpu_offload=true` for top-10 tenants impacted.
maria: Canary applied to worker-42/43 now for kernel preference and kv settings (rolling restart on those nodes). Watching metrics.
kevin: Before/after snapshot: canary nodes show immediate drop in OOMs and no restarts in the first 3m, throughput on those two nodes back to baseline. Other nodes still degraded.
deng: Profiling from canary (alloc-aware kernels): notable differences:
```
# before (fused probing): avg latency (p50/p95) = 28ms / 120ms
# after (alloc-aware pinned):  p50/p95 = 30ms / 85ms
# memory churn: small-alloc ops/sec down 42%
# kernel fallback count: down from 1200 -> 8
```
leo: That's encouraging — the slight increase in p50 is fine vs big p95 improvement and stability. Recommend rolling kernel-preference to 30% of pool and keeping kvcache throttle for 30m to drain fragmentation.
aj: I'll schedule a slow rollout: +10% every 5 minutes with monitoring guardrails (OOMs, restarts, p95). If OOMs drop and restarts stop, we'll keep defaults changed and file a follow-up perf task to fix allocator fragmentation.
maria: After 20m of rollout throughput recovered to ~95% of baseline cluster-wide and OOMs drop to background. Starting collection of full heap profiles and nvprof traces for later analysis.
kevin: Collecting /tmp/heap_snap_worker-*.prof and gpu_mem_map timestamped. Also saving kernel-probe traces to s3://redwood-internal/diagnostics/2019-01-23-hotpage-sweep/
sre-rotation: Good mitigation work. Please open an incident postmortem with timeline, root-cause hypothesis, and action items: 1) short-term: keep kvcache throttle and alloc-aware kernel pin for 48h 2) medium-term: allocator defragmentation work + KV cache eviction smoothing 3) long-term: runtime kernel probe safety improvements and memory compaction. Assigning owners: kevin (data+profiling), deng (kernel/runtime), leo (rollout + canary docs).
maria: Will compile timeline and attach traces. Thanks all — :thumbsup:
